object_description: compact elongated volume with articulated cuts and terraces
design_condition: The volume aligns with the existing administration building, expanding the street into a tree-separated forecourt while creating a coherent sequence of green outdoor spaces and a widening gap that protects adjacent school and kindergarten spaces.

positive.statement: The placement creates a noticeable anteroom and a coherent sequence of attractive outdoor spaces.

position.rationale: Elongated volume and adjacent open forecourt visibly define the approximate anteroom.

positive.statement: The compact volume and minimal east-west extent create useful distance and protected outdoor spaces.

position.target: compact volume and protected outdoor spaces
position.rationale: Compact elongated envelope and narrow east-west extent are corroborated across views.

positive.statement: The volume is shaped by incisions and expansions that articulate entrances, covered play areas, and terraces.

position.target: incisions, entrances, covered play areas, and terraces
position.rationale: Repeated cuts and stepped edge features are visible in top and elevation projections.

positive.statement: The generous skylight supports daylight, clear orientation, and differentiated circulation.

position.rationale: Skylight is not individually resolved; roof ridge is the relevant envelope anchor.

positive.statement: The proposal is extremely convincing in its compactness and offers a coherent architectural concept.

position.rationale: Evaluates the whole compact building concept.

positive.statement: The structural concept promises cost-effective production and the construction approach supports robustness and low maintenance.

position.target: structural concept and robust low-maintenance construction
position.rationale: Structure, cost, and maintenance are global performance judgments.

negative.statement: Conflicts between pedestrians and vehicles are expected at the access to the new building.

position.rationale: Access conflict is not directly represented; lower-west approach is a plausible site anchor.

negative.statement: The use of the building is not sufficiently noticeable in its expression.

position.rationale: Use identity is judged at the visible elongated facade without a distinct program marker.

negative.statement: The effect of the materials on the attractiveness of the spaces for children is questioned.

position.rationale: Material effects are not resolved; lower facade offers an approximate children’s-space anchor.

negative.statement: Reducing the number of outdoor parking spaces could clarify and separate pedestrian and vehicle access.

position.rationale: Parking is absent; eastern lower forecourt marks a plausible access zone.

negative.statement: It must be carefully examined how the fire-protection requirements can be fully met.

position.rationale: Fire-protection compliance is an unlocated technical judgment.
